safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 4.0 days to 2.0 days

narrative: Material PL1__ME83C4D0 exhibits continuous demand averaging 405.71 units per working day with moderate variability (CV=0.36) and a statistically significant upward trend of +31.7% over the observation period. Lead times average 2.92 days with moderate instability (CV=0.36), driven primarily by transport variance. The (r,Q) policy with reorder point 2,002 and order quantity 4,813 achieves the 95% service level while respecting the 5,685.82-unit storage ceiling, leaving only 56 units of headroom.
warnings: SAP safety stock (82 units) is critically under-dimensioned — ~10x below the statistically required level of 817 units
Significant upward demand trend (+31.7%) detected — static EOQ may underestimate forward requirements within 3-6 months
Storage utilization reaches 99% (5,630 of 5,686 units) — capacity cap binds the order quantity
SAP safety lead time of 4.0 days exceeds the statistically justified 2.0 days — recommend reduction

research_insights.selection_rationale: Continuous high-frequency demand (98.9% non-zero days) with moderate CV and a detectable trend makes a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. It triggers replenishment precisely when stock hits the reorder point, minimising stockout exposure without the overhead of periodic review cycles. EOQ balances ordering and holding costs at the observed demand rate.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage capacity cap (5,685.82 units) binds the policy: unconstrained EOQ would be 4,813 units but combined with SS=817 this consumes 99% of capacity. Any demand acceleration from the detected trend will quickly exhaust available headroom, risking either stockouts (if replenishment is delayed) or a capacity breach. A capacity expansion review is recommended if the demand trend persists.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility. MOQ (656) + SS (817) = 1,473 units, well within 5,685.82. Capacity constraint is satisfied but with minimal margin.
